A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same X-Fi research. All pages, including appendices, are readable, and the equations, tables and figures can be matched across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original HPE and HAR experiments on MM-Fi and XRF55, including quantitative comparisons, ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, component ablations and a continual-learning experiment in the appendix.

M1.justification: The encoders, key-value generators, iterative X-Fusion, pooling, task losses and modality-drop training remain unchanged. Renamed cross-attention modules, expanded explanations and experiments with alternative configurations do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The datasets, HPE/HAR tasks and sensor modalities remain unchanged. Appendix A.6 adds a limited continual-learning scenario: incorporating mmWave after initial RGB/depth training, extending evaluation beyond combinations drawn from the original jointly trained modality set.

E2.justification: Appendix A.3 and Table 7 add actual comparisons with ImmFusion and Meta-Transformer-B16F/B16T, substantially extending the external comparator set. The Visual Odometry Transformer in Tables 4–5 matches v1's transformer-fusion comparator in architecture description and scores; its relabeling is not an additional baseline.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce staged modality fine-tuning, frozen-versus-trainable Meta-Transformer configurations, and controlled key-value, iteration-count, transformer-depth and training-loss comparisons. These substantially extend evaluation design. The named dataset splits and default four X-Fusion iterations clarify existing experiments; they do not establish changed settings or reruns.

E4.justification: v3 retains the earlier ablations and adds tests of key-value generators, two versus four iterations, and one versus four transformer layers (Table 8). It also adds continual-learning and parameter-count analyses, RGB/depth sample diagnostics, and pooling/contrastive-loss training curves (Figure 8). Figure 5 enlarges an existing pose example.

E5.justification: Both versions describe the main X-Fi results as averages from multiple experiments without specifying run counts or seeds. v3 introduces no standard deviations, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: All seven original tables retain their numerical values, with v1 Table 7 becoming v3 Table 11; Figures 3–4 are also unchanged. New Tables 7–10 and Figure 8 substantially expand results. For example, five-modality HPE adds ImmFusion and Meta-Transformer-B16T MPJPEs of 107.9 and 91.4 mm against the retained X-Fi result of 83.7 mm. Table 9 reports mixed effects of continual fine-tuning.

T1.justification: The model equations and independent-binomial modality-sampling formulation are mathematically unchanged apart from notation. Added explanations of dimensions and implicit alignment introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: training once for flexible combinations of participating modalities, preserving modality-specific information through X-Fusion, and state-of-the-art HPE/HAR performance. Additional evidence does not change these claims' scope.

C2.justification: v3 refines the fusion rationale from ensuring equal attention to recovering overlooked modality information, and explains pooling/dropout as implicit alignment. Appendix A.5 attributes RGB/depth limb-estimation differences to motion blur and contour visibility. New ablation interpretations favor four over two iterations and one over four transformer layers.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access pointer, identifies MM-Fi's S1 Random Split and XRF55's original split, and states the default four X-Fusion iterations. It also documents new baseline fine-tuning configurations and fusion-block parameter counts. Existing backbone, optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 substantially expands positioning around cross-modal distillation, joint embeddings and foundation models, adding work such as CLIP, ImageBind, PaLM-E and Meta-Transformer while removing the OneLLM discussion. It revises decision-level fusion's limitation from fixed combinations to possible degradation from weak modalities, and identifies the retained transformer comparison with Memmel et al. (2023).

P1.justification: v3 standardizes notation and terminology, edits grammar, rewrites selected related-work and mechanism passages, and adds descriptive appendix subsections. Publication and affiliation text also changes. The main section sequence and most existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 gain explicit training stages, component labels and clearer grouping. New Tables 7–10 and Figures 5–8 add comparison tables, diagnostic imagery, a component diagram and training curves, substantially expanding visual presentation. Existing tables and Figures 3–4 are retained; the earlier Table 7 is relocated as Table 11.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens support for the central performance and design claims through direct ImmFusion/Meta-Transformer comparisons and targeted component ablations absent from v1. Split and default-setting disclosures plus a code-access pointer improve reproducibility. These address important validation gaps despite unchanged headline results. Continual-learning outcomes are mixed, and statistical uncertainty remains unquantified.
